about: p05-ipc queue targets (plans/cmux-next/chrome-parity/p05-ipc.md, section 6). scripts/cmux-next/ipc-census.py --record writes `base`; --check fails when a queue grows past it or an allowlist entry has no reason or matches no site. Allowlist entries are {queue, file, key (optional: the whole file), reason}. Task p05-ipc-106 adds the transient daemon connections of section 3.1. `ipc5_ops` lists the IPC-5 ops; cmux-tui/scripts/bench-daemon-latency.py `--ops all` measures each of them and refuses to run when one has no plan. `runtime.Q16` (items {file, line, key, p95_ms, wire}) and `runtime.Q16_run` (command, scenario, threshold_ms, sha, host, daemon_version, skipped, failed) are written by `bench-daemon-latency.py --ops all --scenario scale --write-q16` on a macOS fleet host (p05-ipc-002); ipc-census.py reads Q16 from there. p05-ipc-128 recorded the Q9 run: `runtime.Q9` (items {file, line, key}, read by ipc-census.py for Q9 and Q18) and `runtime.Q9_run` (sha, host, command, runs); `triage.Q9` gives every (kind, site) of that run a `task` (`tasks.Q9` defines the p05-ipc-3NN ones; others are existing tasks), a `reason`, or both; `why` holds the backtrace that ties a site to its task.

allowlist.reason: The transport's own socket: every LineTransport is already a Q4 site at its constructor.
Not a cmux-tui daemon socket: the CUA host's line socket.
Not a cmux-tui daemon socket: acpmux's unix socket (_acpmux/watch).
Not a cmux-tui daemon socket: the acpmux server peer check.
Not a cmux-tui daemon socket: acpmux's _acpmux/status call.
Not a cmux-tui daemon socket: the peer stamp of the acpmux socket.
Not a cmux-tui daemon socket: the browser host's provider socket.
Not a cmux-tui daemon socket: another cmux app's control socket.
Not a cmux-tui daemon socket: the stale-file probe of the app's own control socket.
Not a cmux-tui daemon socket: the Tasks owner (cmux task serve).
Not a Q8 thread: spawn_cloud_reader_with passes the closure the name machine-agent-cloud-reader-{generation}.

The relay forwards a page's runtime-named op unchanged (react-pages.md 1.1) and the daemon validates its params against the catalog, as Chromium routes WebUI chrome.send messages by name (content/browser/webui/web_ui_impl.cc); no generated type can name an op chosen at run time.
The typed funnel itself: it sends a generated ResourceRequestLine through DaemonConnection's one resource request path (p05-ipc-045).

Q9_run.host: cmux-orchestrator-1 (Linux 7.0.0-1014-gcp x86_64, 360 cores), debug test build
Q9_run.command: cd cmux-tui && CMUX_TUI_REQUEST_PATH_IO=record cargo test -p cmux-tui-core 2>&1 | grep REQUEST_PATH_IO | sort | uniq -c

runs.what: the command as written: lib tests
runs.result: 83 sites. 207 lib tests failed and cargo stopped before the integration targets; the 8 server::capabilities::ipc_grant_tests hang on Linux and were killed after every other test ended.

runs.what: each test binary on its own (lib minus ipc_grant_tests, and the 20 tests/*.rs targets)
runs.result: 165 sites, a superset of the first run's. With the thread blocking detector panicking (its Debug default), mux-line-out panics at server/outbound_batch.rs:57 (condvar-wait), which fails most socket tests before their handlers run. In record mode all 20 integration targets pass and the lib has 3245 passed, 246 failed, 14 ignored.

Q9_run.notes: Linux run: proc_scan sites read /proc here, sysctl or proc_pidinfo on macOS, at the same call sites. lock_hold_over_1ms depends on timing, so a fleet run can show a different subset of the sqlite sites. Backtraces for the non-sqlite sites come from CMUX_TUI_REQUEST_PATH_IO=panic:<kind> runs with RUST_BACKTRACE=1.

Q9.title: Q9 proc_scan: terminal-resources samples off the request thread
Q9.change: Sites terminal_resources.rs:11 (Sampler::new) and :94 (sampler.sample): terminal-resources walks and samples the process table inside the request's RequestPathScope. Post the walk to a background sequence outside any request scope and reply from its completion, as Chrome's task manager refreshes process metrics on a blocking-allowed background sequence and posts the result back (chrome/browser/task_manager/sampling/task_group_sampler.cc). Still one sample per request: no cache, no timer.
Q9.acceptance: A Q9 record run has no proc_scan site in terminal_resources.rs; request_path_io.proc_scan == 0 after a terminal-resources call; tests/terminal_resources.rs passes.

Q9.title: Q9 proc_scan: closing a pane reads no process table
Q9.change: Site terminal_archive.rs:197: every terminal a close-pane closes calls platform::foreground_job_name on the request thread (cmd_panes.rs:295 -> batch_close.rs:607 -> terminal_archive.rs:76). Take the stopped job's name from the foreground process the terminal host already reports (add it to that report if it is missing) instead of a process table read at close.
Q9.acceptance: A Q9 record run has no proc_scan site in terminal_archive.rs; close-pane and close-surface have request_path_io.proc_scan == 0; a reopened stopped job keeps its name (archive tests pass).
